Retrieved via Exa 19 July 2026. Reuters wire copy carried by approved-adjacent syndication partners; sourcing is Reuters newsroom.

SATURDAY 18 JULY (Reuters):
- US said two personnel killed in Jordan, another missing, after Iranian attack. Seventh straight night of US strikes.
- Iran targeted Saudi Arabia plus other US Gulf allies and Jordan on Saturday. Saudi early-warning alerts in al-Kharj (east of Riyadh, hosts US troops) and Yanbu (Red Sea oil export terminal) — first Saudi alerts in more than three months.
- Kuwait under sustained attack: armed forces intercepted Iranian ballistic missiles and drones; some firefighters and oil-sector workers injured while responding. Kuwait Petroleum Corporation said one oil facility was damaged in "repeated Iranian attacks." A power generation and water desalination plant hit (second attack on Kuwaiti desalination sites in two days). Kuwait International Airport operations suspended due to repeated missile/drone threats.
- IRGC: struck Camp Arifjan and a facility at Ali Al Salem Air Base (Kuwait); targeted Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain (US combat aircraft) and an intelligence/AI data centre; claimed it destroyed at least two US fighter aircraft and three other aircraft in the early-Saturday attack on Al Azraq base, Jordan (per Iranian state TV).
- US airstrikes early Saturday killed three and wounded eight in Hormozgan province; two bridges and a road tunnel damaged (Iranian state TV). Further US strikes Saturday afternoon in same province (Fars), no reported civilian casualties.
- OIL: prices climbed more than 4% to their highest level in over a month (News24/Reuters). [Context: Brent ~$88.10 as of Fri 17 July close per Trading Economics; up >14% on the week.]
- The EU and Gulf states called on Iran to immediately and unconditionally halt all attacks and interference with maritime navigation and keep the strait open without conditions or fees (joint statement, Saudi state TV, Saturday).
- US said forces redirected four commercial vessels, disabled one, and boarded another to enforce its naval blockade of Iran. Fars published a list of five ports (Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, UAE) it said could become targets.
